readings.title: Rachel Weeping for Her Children
readings.subtitle: A promise of return from the land of the enemy and an end to weeping.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 31:15] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing, bitter weeping, Raḥěl weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”
[16] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Hold back <dn>את</dn> your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and they shall return from the land of the enemy.</dq>
[17] <dq>“And there is expectancy for your latter end,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and your children shall return to their own country.</dq>
[18] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have clearly heard <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim lamenting, ‘You have chastised me, and <dn>I</dn> was chastised, like an untrained calf. Turn me back, and <dn>I</dn> shall turn back, for You are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[19] <dq>For after <dn>my</dn> turning back, <dn>I</dn> repented. And after <dn>I</dn> was instructed, <dn>I</dn> struck myself on the thigh. <dn>I</dn> was ashamed, even humiliated, for <dn>I</dn> bore the reproach of <dn>my</dn> youth.’</dq>
[20] <dq>“Is Ephrayim a precious son to <dn>Me</dn>, a child of delights? For though <dn>I</dn> spoke against him, <dn>I</dn> still remembered him. That is why <dn>My</dn> affections were deeply moved for him. <dn>I</dn> have great compassion for him,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[21] <dq>“Set up signposts, make landmarks; set your heart toward the highway, the way in which you went. Turn back, O maiden of Yisra’ěl, turn back to these cities of yours!</dq>
[22] <dq>“Till when would you turn here and there, O backsliding daughter? For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has created <dn>את</dn> what is new on earth: a woman encompasses a man!”</dq>

readings.title: A Blessed and Righteous Dwelling
readings.subtitle: The promise of replenishment and the principle of individual accountability.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 31:23] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Let them once again say <dn>את</dn> this word in the land of Yehuḏah and in its cities, when <dn>I</dn> turn back their captivity, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> bless you, O home of righteousness, mountain of set-apartness!’</dq>
[24] <dq>“And in Yehuḏah and all its cities farmers and those who journey with flocks, shall dwell together.</dq>
[25] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> shall fill the weary being, and <dn>I</dn> shall replenish every grieved being.”</dq>
[26] At this I awoke and looked around, and my sleep was sweet to me.
[27] <dq>“See, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that <dn>I</dn> shall sow <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ěl and <dn>את</dn> the house of Yehuḏah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.</dq>
[28] <dq>“And it shall be, that as <dn>I</dn> have watched over them to pluck up, and to break down, and to throw down, and to destroy, and to afflict, so <dn>I</dn> shall watch over them to build and to plant,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[29] <dq>“In those days they shall no longer say, ‘The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are blunted.’</dq>
[30] <dq>“But each one shall die for his own crookedness – whoever eats sour grapes, his teeth shall be blunted.</dq>

readings.title: A Renewed Covenant Written on the Heart
readings.subtitle: The promise of an internal Torah, universal knowledge of YeHoVaH, and forgiveness of sin.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 31:31] <dq>“See, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“when <dn>I</dn> shall make a renewed covenant with <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ěl and with <dn>את</dn> the house of Yehuḏah,</dq>
[32] <dq>not like the covenant <dn>I</dn> made with their fathers in the day when <dn>I</dn> strengthened their hand to bring them out of the land of Mitsrayim, <dn>My</dn> covenant which they broke, though <dn>I</dn> was a husband to them,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[33] <dq>“For this is the covenant <dn>I</dn> shall make with the house of Yisra’ěl after those days,</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: <dq><dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Torah in their inward parts, and write it on their hearts. And <dn>I</dn> shall be their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and they shall be <dn>My</dn> people.</dq>
[34] <dq>“And no longer shall they teach, each one his neighbour, and each one his brother, saying, ‘Know <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,’ for they shall all know <dn>Me</dn>, from the least of them to the greatest of them,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> shall forgive their crookedness, and remember their sin no more.”</dq>
[35] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the laws of the moon and the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea, and its waves roar – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name:
[36] <dq>“If these laws vanish from before <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“then the seed of Yisra’ěl shall also cease from being a nation before <dn>Me</dn> forever.”</dq>
[37] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“If the heavens above could be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, <dn>I</dn> would also cast off <dn>את</dn> all the seed of Yisra’ěl for all that they have done,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Jerusalem Rebuilt and Set-Apart
readings.subtitle: The city's boundaries will be extended and consecrated to YeHoVaH forever.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 31:38] <dq>“See, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that the city shall be built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the Tover of Ḥanan’ěl to the Corner Gate.</dq>
[39] <dq>“And the measuring line shall again extend straight ahead to the hill Garěḇ, then it shall turn toward Go‛ah.</dq>
[40] <dq>“And all the valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields as far as the wadi Qiḏron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, is to be set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It shall not be plucked up or thrown down any more forever.”</dq>

readings.title: The Breaking of Elam's Bow
readings.subtitle: A prophecy of scattering and destruction, followed by a promise of future restoration.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 49:34] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that came to Yirmeyahu the prophet concerning Ěylam, in the beginning of the reign of Tsiḏqiyah, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying,
[35] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am breaking <dn>את</dn> the bow of Ěylam, the chief of their might.</dq>
[36] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall bring upon Ěylam <dn>את</dn> the four winds from the four quarters of the heavens, and scatter them toward all those winds. And there shall be no nation where the outcasts of Ěylam do not go.</dq>
[37] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> Ěylam before their enemies and before those who seek their life. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring evil upon them, <dn>my</dn> burning displeasure,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> the sword after them until <dn>I</dn> have consumed them.</dq>
[38] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> throne in Ěylam, and destroy from there <dn>את</dn> the sovereign and the heads,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[39] <dq>And it shall be in the latter days that <dn>I</dn> turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Ěylam,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”

readings.title: The Fall of Babylon Announced
readings.subtitle: A nation from the north will desolate the land of the Kasdim.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:1] The word that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke concerning Baḇel, concerning the land of the Kasdim by Yirmeyahu the prophet.
[2] <dq>“Declare among the nations, and let it be heard. And lift up a banner, let it be heard, and do not conceal it. Say, ‘Baḇel shall be taken, Běl shall be put to shame, Meroḏaḵ shall be broken, her images shall be put to shame, her idols shall be broken.’</dq>
[3] <dq>For a nation shall come up against her from the north, which shall make her land waste, and none shall dwell in it. They shall flee, they shall go, both man and beast.</dq>

readings.title: Israel and Judah Seek YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: In the time of Babylon's fall, the scattered people will return and join themselves to an everlasting covenant.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:4] <dq>“In those days and at that time,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“the children of Yisra’ěl shall come, they and the children of Yehuḏah together, weeping as they come, and seek <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[5] <dq>“They shall ask the way to Tsiyon, their faces toward it, ‘Come and let us join ourselves to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in an everlasting covenant, never to be forgotten.’</dq>
[6] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> people have been wandering sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray, turning them away on the mountains. They have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their resting place.</dq>
[7] <dq>“All who found them have devoured them. And their adversaries have said, ‘We are not guilty, because they have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Home of righteousness, and the Expectation of their fathers: <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq>
[8] <dq>“Flee from the midst of Baḇel, come out of the land of the Kasdim. And be as rams before a flock.</dq>
[9] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am stirring up and bringing up against Baḇel <dn>את</dn> an assembly of great nations from a land of the north, and they shall array themselves against her. From there she shall be captured – their arrows are like those of a mighty skilled man, not returning empty-handed.</dq>
[10] <dq>“And Chaldea shall become plunder, all who plunder her shall satisfy themselves,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Plunderer Plundered
readings.subtitle: Babylon, who rejoiced in plundering God's inheritance, will become a desolate wilderness.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:11] <dq>“Because you were glad, because you rejoiced, you who plunder <dn>My</dn> inheritance, because you have grown fat like a heifer threshing grain, and you neigh like stallions,</dq>
[12] <dq>your mother shall be greatly ashamed. She who bore you shall be humiliated. Look, the last of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land and a desert.</dq>
[13] <dq>“Because of the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> she shall not be inhabited, but she shall be deserted – all of it. Everyone passing by Baḇel shall be astonished and whistle at all her plagues.</dq>
[14] <dq>“Set yourselves in array against Baḇel all around, all you who bend the bow. Shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[15] <dq>“Shout against her all around. She has given her hand, her foundations have fallen, her walls are thrown down, for it is the vengeance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Take vengeance on her. As she has done, so do to her.</dq>
[16] <dq>"Cut off <dn>את</dn> the sower from Baḇel, and him who handles the sickle at harvest time. From before the sword of the oppressor each one turns to his own people, and each one flees to his own land.</dq>

readings.title: Vengeance for Scattered Israel
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH will punish Babylon as He punished Assyria, and He will restore and pardon the remnant of His people.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:17] “Yisra’ěl is a scattered sheep, the lions have driven him away. First the sovereign of Ashshur devoured him, and now, at last, this Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel has broken his bones.”
[18] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am punishing <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Baḇel and his land, as <dn>I</dn> have punished <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ashshur.</dq>
[19] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring back <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl to his pasture, and he shall feed on Karmel and Bashan. And his being shall be satisfied on Mount Ephrayim and Gil‛aḏ.</dq>
[20] <dq>“In those days and at that time,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“the crookedness of Yisra’ěl shall be searched for, but there shall be none; and the sin of Yehuḏah, but none shall be found. For <dn>I</dn> shall pardon those whom <dn>I</dn> leave as a remnant.</dq>

readings.title: The Hammer of the Earth is Broken
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH opens His armory to execute His work against the proud land of Babylon.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:21] <dq>“Go up against the land of Merathayim, against it, and against the inhabitants of Peqoḏ. Slay and put them under the ban,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and do according to all that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you.</dq>
[22] <dq>“There is a sound of battle in the land, and of great destruction.</dq>
[23] <dq>“How the hammer of all the earth has been cut off and broken! How Baḇel has become a ruin among the nations!</dq>
[24] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have laid a snare for you, and you were captured, O Baḇel, and you yourself did not know! You have been found and also caught, because you strove against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
[25] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has opened <dn>His</dn> armoury, and has brought out <dn>את</dn> the weapons of <dn>His</dn> displeasure, for the Master <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts has a work to do in the land of the Kasdim.
[26] <dq>Come against her from every quarter, open her storehouses, pile her up as heaps of ruins, and put her under the ban. Let her have no remnant.</dq>
[27] <dq>Slay all her bulls, let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them! For their day has come, the time of their punishment.</dq>
[28] <dq>Listen! They flee and escape from the land of Baḇel, to declare in Tsiyon <dn>את</dn> the vengeance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, the vengeance of <dn>His</dn> Hěḵal.</dq>
[29] <dq>“Summon archers against Baḇel. All you who bend the bow, encamp against it all around, let no one escape. Repay her according to her work, do to her according to all she has done. For she has been proud against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, against the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl.</dq>
[30] <dq>“Therefore her young men shall fall in the streets, and all her men of battle shall perish in that day,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[31] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you, O proud one!”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“for your day has come, the time for your punishment.</dq>
[32] <dq>“And the proud one shall stumble, and he shall fall, with no one to raise him up. And <dn>I</dn> shall kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all around him.”</dq>

readings.title: The Strong Redeemer
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH will plead the case of His oppressed people and bring unrest to the inhabitants of Babylon.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:33] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, “The children of Yisra’ěl were oppressed, along with the children of Yehuḏah. And all who took them captive have held them fast, they refused to let them go.
[34] “Their Redeemer is strong, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name. <dn>He</dn> shall strongly plead their case, so as to give rest to the land, but unrest to the inhabitants of Baḇel.
[35] “A sword is upon the Kasdim,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “and it is upon the inhabitants of Baḇel, and upon her heads and upon her wise men.
[36] “A sword is upon the liars, and they shall be fools. A sword is upon her mighty men, and they shall be broken down.
[37] “A sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mixed peoples who are in her midst, and they shall become like women. A sword is upon her treasures, and they shall be plundered.
[38] “A sword is upon her waters, and they shall be dried up. For it is a land of carved images, and they boast about their idols.
[39] “Therefore the wild desert beasts shall dwell with the jackals, and the ostriches dwell in it. And it shall never again be inhabited, nor dwelt in, unto all generations.
[40] “As <dn>Elohim</dn> overthrew <dn>את</dn> Seḏom and Amorah and their neighbouring cities,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “so no one would dwell there, nor would son of man sojourn in it.

readings.title: The Invader from the North
readings.subtitle: A great nation and many sovereigns are stirred up from the ends of the earth against Babylon.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 50:41] “See, a people shall come from the north, and a great nation and many sovereigns stirred up from the ends of the earth.
[42] “They strengthen their bow and spear, they are cruel and they show no compassion. They sound like the roaring sea, and ride on horses, set in array, like a man for the battle, against you, O daughter of Baḇel.
[43] “The sovereign of Baḇel has heard the report about them, and his hands became weak. Distress has taken hold of him, pain like that of a woman in labour.
[44] “See, he comes up like a lion from the Yarděn jungle, against the enduring pasture. But in an instant <dn>I</dn> shall make them run away from her. And who is the Chosen One whom <dn>I</dn> appoint against her? For who is like <dn>Me</dn>? Who summons <dn>Me</dn>? And who is that Shepherd who stands before <dn>Me</dn>?”
[45] Therefore hear <dn>את</dn> the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> has counselled concerning Baḇel, and <dn>His</dn> purposes <dn>He</dn> has purposed concerning the land of the Kasdim: the least of the flock shall drag them away! <dn>He</dn> shall make their pasture a waste before them!
[46] At the sound of Baḇel’s capture the earth shall be shaken, and the outcry shall be heard among the nations.

readings.title: The Winnowing of Babylon
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH stirs up a destroyer and calls the Medes to execute His vengeance for His Temple.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 51:1] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am stirring up <dn>את</dn> the spirit of a destroyer against Baḇel, against those who dwell in Lěb – <dn>My</dn> opponents.</dq>
[2] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall send winnowers to Baḇel, who shall winnow her and empty her land. For they shall be against her all around, in the day of evil.</dq>
[3] <dq>“Let the archer draw his bow, and let him stand ready in his armour. Do not spare her young men, put all her army under the ban.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And the slain shall fall in the land of the Kasdim, and the pierced-through in her streets.</dq>
[5] <dq>“For neither Yisra’ěl nor Yehuḏah is widowed by his <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, though their land has been filled with sin against the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl.”</dq>
[6] Flee from the midst of Baḇel, and let each one save his life! Do not be cut off in her crookedness, for this is the time of the vengeance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the recompense <dn>He</dn> is repaying her.
[7] Baḇel was a golden cup in the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, making drunk all the earth. The nations drank her wine, that is why the nations went mad!
[8] Baḇel shall suddenly fall and be broken. Howl for her! Take balm for her pain – if so be, she might be healed.
[9] We would have healed Baḇel, but she is not healed. Let us leave her and each go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens and is lifted up to the clouds.
[10] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought forth our righteousness. Come and let us relate in Tsiyon <dn>את</dn> the work of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[11] Polish the arrows! Put on the shields! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has stirred up <dn>את</dn> the spirit of the sovereigns of the Medes. For <dn>His</dn> plan is against Baḇel to destroy it, because it is the vengeance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the vengeance for <dn>His</dn> Hěḵal.
[12] Lift up a banner on the walls of Baḇel, strengthen the watch, station the watchmen, prepare the ambush. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has both planned and done what <dn>He</dn> spoke concerning the inhabitants of Baḇel.
[13] You who dwell upon many waters, great in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your greedy gain.
[14] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts has sworn by <dn>Himself</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall certainly fill you with men, as with locusts, and they shall lift up a shout against you.”</dq>
